sections.text: Yes, sir!
We wrap FFmpeg. Then we wrap the audio files. Then we wrap the wrapper around the files and the files around the wrapper.
Of course, a wrapper needs a proper wrapper, so we wrap that too.
Then we wrap everything in a user interface, wrap some metadata around it, and add another layer of wrapping, just in case.
At this point, nobody really knows what's inside anymore.
But it has more layers than a burrito.
And if something doesn't work, we just wrap it again.

question: What do you do for a living?

sections.text: I'm a social educator working on a project called Edible City, together with twelve wonderful people who need a little extra support in their lives.
We're creating a beautiful public garden where everyone is welcome. Anyone can stop by, pick fresh vegetables, enjoy the flowers, or simply sit down and relax. Everything is free.
We grow vegetables, plant flowers, trees and shrubs, build birdhouses and insect hotels, and generally try to make the world a slightly nicer place.
My office is a tiny construction trailer right in the middle of it all.
We also have plans for world domination.
But that sounds like an awful lot of work.
So we usually just have a barbecue instead.
Yes. Quite a lot, actually.
Artificial intelligence helped write parts of BookStitch, fix bugs, create icons, and occasionally introduce entirely new problems nobody had asked for.
BookStitch itself doesn't use artificial intelligence to process your audiobooks. It relies on traditional algorithms, FFmpeg, and a rather unreasonable amount of optimism.
The developer also claims to possess some intelligence of his own. This has not yet been independently verified.
Nevertheless, he insists he knows what he's doing.
The AI has declined to comment.
First of all, believe in yourself.
At BookStitch, we believe that every challenge is an opportunity to grow, learn, and discover the strength that already lies within you.
You are capable of so much more than you think.
When things don't work out, don't give up. Take a moment, trust your abilities, and remind yourself that every problem is simply another step on your journey.
Don't let error messages, unexpected crashes, or the doubts of others discourage you.
You have everything you need to succeed. Sometimes all it takes is a little patience, a positive attitude, and the courage to believe in yourself.
Remember, the most important tool is not your computer.
It's you.
And we believe in you.
You've got this.
Barely Operational Overengineered Kilobyte Stitching Technology Involving Terrible Coding Habits.

question: I don't like BookStitch. Other programs are better!

sections.text: That's not a question.
Other programs have larger development teams, professional designers, extensive documentation, and actual budgets.
BookStitch has one developer, a garden, a construction trailer, and a rather unhealthy relationship with FFmpeg.
Frankly, I'm surprised it works at all.
